holidays.name: National Skyscraper Day
holidays.description: A day to look up and admire the towering steel-and-glass giants that scrape the sky and give pigeons million-dollar views.
holidays.origin: Observed on the birthday of Louis Henry Sullivan, born September 3, 1856, who is often called the 'father of skyscrapers' and mentored Frank Lloyd Wright.
holidays.funFact: Sullivan coined the phrase 'form follows function,' which became a guiding mantra of modern architecture.

holidays.name: National Welsh Rarebit Day
holidays.description: A celebration of cheesy, saucy goodness poured over toast. Despite the name, there is no bunny involved, just melted cheese, mustard, and beer or ale.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday honoring the classic dish from Wales, which dates back to at least the 1700s, when 'Welsh rabbit' was a cheeky name for a meatless meal.
holidays.funFact: The name was originally 'Welsh rabbit,' likely as a joke implying that the Welsh were so poor they had to eat cheese instead of meat. 'Rarebit' came later.

holidays.name: National Ounce Day
holidays.description: A day for appreciating small measurements, from ounces of gold to ounces of prevention. A perfect excuse to weigh everything you own, just because.
holidays.origin: A lighthearted unofficial observance celebrating the humble ounce, a unit of weight with roots in ancient Rome's 'uncia,' meaning one-twelfth.
holidays.funFact: The word 'ounce' comes from the Latin 'uncia,' and the abbreviation 'oz' comes from the Italian word 'onza.'

holidays.name: Eat an Extra Dessert Day
holidays.description: A sweet-toothed rebellion where seconds on dessert are not only allowed but encouraged. Calories do not count, according to the unofficial rules.
holidays.origin: A food-lover's observance popularized through online holiday calendars, designed to give dessert enthusiasts a guilt-free excuse to indulge.
holidays.funFact: The word 'dessert' comes from the French 'desservir,' meaning 'to clear the table,' since sweets were originally served after the main meal was cleared away.

holidays.name: Bring Your Teddy Bear to Work Day
holidays.description: A cuddly workplace tradition where employees invite their stuffed pals to the office for moral support, stress relief, and surprisingly productive meetings.
holidays.origin: Part of a playful trend of 'bring your' workplace observances, encouraging lighthearted fun and reduced stress on the job.
holidays.funFact: The teddy bear was named after President Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt, after he refused to shoot a captured bear on a 1902 hunting trip.
